key_insight: DeepFEAv2 extends transient finite element surrogate modeling beyond structured meshes by jointly predicting node- and element-based outputs over time.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable way to accelerate transient FEA for complex mesh topologies and element types while preserving high predictive accuracy.
method: Uses the FE connectivity matrix to group features by element and build a topology-guided input sequence.
Employs a neural architecture that processes this sequence to jointly predict node and element outputs across time.
Adds an FEA-informed regularization strategy to improve physical consistency of the predicted fields.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on structured and unstructured 3D linear elastic datasets plus a pressure-driven aortic valve case, reaching R² up to 0.99, normalized error as low as 0.38%, and up to three orders of magnitude faster inference than traditional FEA.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate mesh connectivity and careful handling of diverse mesh topologies and element types.
paper_title: DeepFEAv2: Deep Learning for Transient Finite Element Analysis Beyond Structured Meshes
